title: Clauses
description: Learn clauses for Grade 7: independent and dependent clauses, and the three kinds of subordinate clause — noun, adjective (relative) and adverb — with bilingual notes, practice and tests.

topics.title: Noun & Adjective Clauses
topics.concept:
A noun clause does the work of a noun. It can be the subject, the object, or the complement.

  • Subject: What she said surprised us.
  • Object: I know that he is right.
  • Complement: The truth is that he failed.

An adjective (relative) clause describes a noun and usually begins with a relative pronoun (who, which, that, whose) or a relative adverb (where, when).

  • The boy who sits next to me is my friend. (describes 'boy')
  • This is the house where I was born. (describes 'house')

A defining relative clause (no commas) is essential; a non-defining one (with commas) just adds extra information: My brother, who lives in Pune, is a doctor.

examples.problem: Identify the noun clause: I don't know where he lives.
examples.solution: where he lives — it is the object of 'know' (a noun clause).

examples.problem: Identify the adjective clause: The pen that you gave me is lost.
examples.solution: that you gave me — it describes the noun 'pen'.

recap: Noun clause = does a noun's job (subject/object/complement)
Defining = no commas (essential); non-defining = commas (extra info)

topics.title: Adverb Clauses
topics.concept:
An adverb clause does the work of an adverb — it tells when, where, why, how, or under what condition. It begins with a subordinating conjunction.

ShowsConjunctionsExample
Timewhen, while, after, before, as soon asCall me when you arrive.
Reasonbecause, since, asHe left because he was tired.
Conditionif, unless, providedYou'll pass if you work hard.
Concessionalthough, even thoughAlthough it rained, we played.
Purpose / Resultso that; so…thatHe ran so that he could catch the bus.

examples.problem: What does this adverb clause show: We waited until the rain stopped.?
examples.solution: Time — 'until the rain stopped' tells when we waited.

examples.problem: Identify the adverb clause and its type: She was happy because she won.
examples.solution: because she won — an adverb clause of reason.

recap: Adverb clause tells when/where/why/how/under what condition
Types: time, reason, condition, concession, purpose, result

'We stopped because we were tired.' — clause type?
Relative pronoun for things:
'I'll come if I am free.' — the clause shows:

'Although he tried, he lost.' — the clause shows:

Identify the clause type: 'The reason why he left is unknown.'
options: 'why he left' is a noun clause
'why he left' is an adjective clause

questions.q: Spot the error: 'I asked him that what he wanted.'
questions.explanation: A 'wh-' noun clause does not take 'that': 'I asked him what he wanted.'

questions.q: Choose the correctly punctuated non-defining clause.
options: Mr Rao who teaches us maths is strict.
Mr Rao, who teaches us maths, is strict.
Mr Rao, who teaches us maths is strict.
Mr Rao who teaches us maths, is strict.
questions.explanation: Commas on both sides of the non-defining clause.

questions.q: Identify the function: 'That he will win is certain.'
questions.explanation: 'That he will win' is the subject — a noun clause.

questions.q: Which sentence contains an adverb clause of result?
options: He was so weak that he fainted.
He fainted because he was weak.
When he was weak, he fainted.
The man who fainted was weak.

questions.q: Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'The scientist ___ theory changed physics was Einstein.'
questions.explanation: 'whose' shows possession (the theory of the scientist).

questions.q: Reduce the adjective clause: 'The girl who is standing there is my friend.'
options: The girl standing there is my friend.
The girl stood there is my friend.
The girl who standing there is my friend.
The girl is standing there my friend.
questions.explanation: 'who is standing' reduces to the participle 'standing'.

questions.q: Identify the noun clause acting as a complement: 'My belief is that honesty pays.'
questions.explanation: 'that honesty pays' completes the linking verb 'is' — noun clause as complement.

outcomes: Tell an independent clause apart from a dependent one
Identify a noun clause and its job in a sentence
Identify an adverb clause and the relationship it shows
Use clauses to build richer sentences

intro.en: A clause is a group of words with its own subject and verb. An independent clause can stand alone as a sentence; a dependent (subordinate) clause cannot. Dependent clauses do one of three jobs — they act as a noun, an adjective, or an adverb — and that is the heart of this chapter.
intro.hi: उपवाक्य (clause) वह शब्द-समूह है जिसमें अपना कर्ता और क्रिया हो। स्वतंत्र उपवाक्य अकेला वाक्य बन सकता है; आश्रित उपवाक्य नहीं। आश्रित उपवाक्य तीन में से कोई एक काम करते हैं — संज्ञा, विशेषण या क्रिया-विशेषण की तरह — और यही इस अध्याय का सार है।

real_life.situation:
You tell a friend about a film:

You: What I liked most was the ending. The hero, who never gives up, wins because he works as a team.
real_life.why: 'What I liked most' is a noun clause (the subject); 'who never gives up' is an adjective clause (describing the hero); 'because he works as a team' is an adverb clause (the reason). Three clause types in one sentence.

rule_box.html:
ClauseActs asBegins with
Nouna nounthat, what, who, whether, why
Adjective (Relative)an adjectivewho, which, that, whose, where
Adverban adverbbecause, when, if, although, so that
rule_box.formula: Noun clause = a thing · Adjective clause = describes a noun · Adverb clause = how/when/why
rule_box.example: That he is honest (noun) is known to all. The man who called (adjective) left. I'll go if it stops raining (adverb).

quick_test.q: A clause that describes a noun is a/an:
quick_test.explanation: An adjective (relative) clause describes a noun.

common_mistakes.wrong: My father who is a doctor works hard. (extra info, needs commas)
common_mistakes.right: My father, who is a doctor, works hard.
common_mistakes.note: A non-defining clause needs commas on both sides.

common_mistakes.wrong: I know that what he said.
common_mistakes.note: Don't stack 'that' and 'what'; one connector is enough.

common_mistakes.wrong: Although he was tired, but he worked.
common_mistakes.right: Although he was tired, he worked.

reading.passage: What surprised everyone was the result. The student who had failed last year, because he had not studied, now stood first. "I worked hard so that I could prove myself," he said. Although the road was difficult, he never gave up. This is the success that hard work brings.

questions.q: Find the noun clause in the first sentence.
questions.answer: "What surprised everyone" — it is the subject (a noun clause).

questions.q: Identify an adjective (relative) clause.
questions.answer: "who had failed last year" or "that hard work brings" — describing a noun.

questions.q: Find an adverb clause of concession.
questions.answer: "Although the road was difficult" — it shows concession/contrast.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences, each containing a different clause: a noun clause, a defining relative clause, a non-defining relative clause, an adverb clause of time, and one of reason.
writing.example: What I want is rest. The boy who won is here. My friend, who lives in Goa, called. When the bell rings, we leave. We stayed because it rained.

micro_quiz.q: 'I know that he is honest.' — the clause 'that he is honest' is a:
micro_quiz.explanation: It is the object of 'know' → noun clause.

micro_quiz.q: 'The car which I bought is red.' — the underlined clause is:
'We left when the show ended.' — type of clause?
micro_quiz.explanation: 'when the show ended' tells the time → adverb clause.
'if you study' is an adverb clause of condition.

challenge.q: Identify the function of the clause: 'I am sure of what he said.'
challenge.explanation: 'what he said' is a noun clause acting as the object of the preposition 'of'.

challenge.q: Which sentence uses a non-defining clause correctly?
options: My phone which is new broke.
My phone, which is new, broke.
My phone, which is new broke.
My phone which is new, broke.
challenge.explanation: A non-defining clause needs a comma on both sides.

challenge.q: Identify the type: 'He spoke so softly that no one heard.'
